    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersTalokan lime prawn tostadasLime-cured prawns with red onion and coriander on crisp tostadas with avocadoHow to make it400g green prawns, peeled and diced4 limes1 red onion, diced1/2 cup coriander leaves2 avocados12 corn tostadasCover the prawns with lime juice.Leave until opaque, then drain and toss with the onion and coriander.Spread smashed avocado on the tostadas and pile the prawns on top just before serving.Heart-shaped herb plantain chipsPlantain chips with a peanut butter, chilli and lime dip. Herb not includedHow to make it3 green plantains1 L vegetable oil for frying1 tsp salt flakes4 tbsp peanut butter3 tbsp warm water1/4 tsp chilli flakes1 tsp lime juicePeel the plantains and slice very thin.Heat the vegetable oil to 180°C and fry in batches until crisp and golden, then salt well.Whisk the peanut butter with warm water, chilli and lime to a smooth dip and serve alongside.Haiti accra taro fritters with piklizNakia's new life in HaitiHow to make itAs written, serves 4Grated taro mixed with garlic, chilli, spring onion and thyme, fried in spoonfuls until crisp, with a fiery pickled cabbage pikliz.A day ahead, pack a quarter of a shredded cabbage, 1 grated carrot, half a sliced onion and 2 sliced chillies into a jar, cover with 300ml white vinegar and the juice of 1 lime.Grate 600g peeled taro and mix with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 1 chopped chilli, 3 spring onions, thyme, 1 egg, 2 tbsp plain flour and salt.Fry spoonfuls at 175°C for 4 minutes until crisp.Serve with the pikliz.MainsMayan pibil porkAchiote pork in banana leaf, roasted 4 hours, in tortillas. Namor's people are MayaHow to make it1.5kg pork shoulder3 tbsp achiote paste2 oranges3 limes3 banana leaves12 corn tortillas1 red onion, slicedBlend the achiote paste with the orange and two limes' juice and rub over the pork.Wrap the pork in banana leaves.Roast covered at 150°C until it falls apart.Pickle the onion in lime juice while the pork cooks.Shred the pork and serve in warm tortillas with the pickled onion.Queen Ramonda's jollof with grilled chickenAn olive branch. Wakanda forever!How to make itAs written, serves 4Smoky jollof rice cooked in a rich tomato, capsicum and chilli base with thyme, topped with charred spiced chicken thighs and fried onions.Blend 2 red capsicums, 400g canned tomatoes, 1 onion and 1 chilli.Fry 1 sliced onion in oil, add 2 tbsp tomato paste and the blend and cook 15 minutes until thick.Add 400g rinsed long grain rice, 500ml chicken stock, thyme, 1 tsp curry powder and salt, cover tightly and cook gently 30 minutes.Rub 1kg chicken thighs with paprika, garlic and oil and grill 6 minutes a side.SweetsK'uk'ulkan coconut flanCoconut and condensed milk caramel flan, fit for NamorHow to make it150g caster sugar4 eggs400ml coconut milk395g condensed milk1 tsp vanilla extract3 tbsp toasted coconut flakes1 lime, zestedMelt the sugar in a pan until deep amber and pour into a 20cm round dish.Whisk the eggs, coconut milk, condensed milk and vanilla and pour over the caramel.Sit the dish in a roasting tin of hot water and bake at 160°C until just set.Cool, then chill overnight.Run a knife round the edge, turn out and top with toasted coconut and lime zest.DrinksTalokan coconut and lime agua frescaCoconut water, shredded coconut and lime blended, strained and poured over iceHow to make it1 L coconut water100g desiccated coconut3 limes3 tbsp caster sugar1 bunch mint1 bag iceBlend the coconut water, coconut, lime juice and sugar until smooth.Strain through a fine sieve, pressing hard.Chill for an hour.Pour into glasses of ice and garnish with lime wheels and mint.
